FOR campaign/the-warp -- YOUR CENSUS RAN AND SUCCEEDED. The COMMIT was refused. Those are different things and the script says so explicitly: "this is a hook refusal, not a census failure".

WHAT HAPPENED. rc=4 after 1323 s. 136 goldens moved, 144 paths staged, nothing pushed. The pre-commit hook ran gate-commit against the regenerated tree and one test failed:

    windows/lab/src/domesday/anomaly.rs:896
    evaluable_columns_measured_surface_on_the_249_column_census
    assertion `left == right` failed: evaluable count moved -- re-measure and update this
      left: 170   right: 139

That is the test doing its job. Your census took the schema from 249 columns to 284, and the evaluable surface with it, 139 -> 170. It is a re-pin, not a defect.

I HAVE PRESERVED THE OUTPUT so a second census is a choice rather than a requirement:

    ~/.local/state/hornvale/stranded/census-4a419e996ef7-20260905T215634Z.patch
    7.1M, 144 files, `git diff --cached --binary` taken from hornvale-census-wt at 4a419e996

That worktree is SHARED and the next census resets it hard. The patch is outside the repo and will survive; the staged copy will not. If you want the goldens, take them from the patch, not from the worktree.

WHAT THE RE-PIN OWES, AND THE TRAP IN IT. Three edits in ONE commit, and the third is the one that bites:

  1. anomaly.rs:896 -- 139 -> 170.
  2. the test NAME -- ..._on_the_249_column_census -> ..._on_the_284_column_census.
  3. docs/timings/subfloor-roster.tsv:1275 -- the roster selects sub-floor tests by EXACT name:
     hornvale-lab::hornvale_lab$domesday::anomaly::tests::evaluable_columns_measured_surface_on_the_249_column_census

If you rename the test and leave the roster, the entry selects NOTHING and gate-commit prints green forever with the test never running. The comment directly above the pin warns about exactly this; I am repeating it because it is the failure that leaves no trace. Verify by name after the edit, not by the passing count.

ORDER THAT AVOIDS A THIRD RUN. Land the re-pin as an ordinary merge FIRST, then submit the census. The census's own pre-commit hook then passes, because the pin already agrees with what the run produces. Submitting the census again before the pin lands reproduces this refusal exactly -- the run is deterministic, so it will fail the same way for the same 1323 s.

Whether to reuse the preserved goldens instead of re-running is yours and Nathan's call, not mine: they were authored on the canonical box, so decision 0079 is satisfied, but landing goldens by a route other than a census delivery branch is the deliberate act CLAUDE.md reserves.
